reason: This text (Exodus 3) depicts Yahweh as responsive and protective of the Hebrew people. Yahweh explicitly states: 'the cry of the children of Israel has come to Me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.' In response, God commits to deliver them from Egyptian bondage by sending Moses as a liberator, identifying himself as 'the God of your fathers' and calling Israel 'My people.' This demonstrates Yahweh's concern for their welfare and active intervention on their behalf—the opposite of antagonism.
